data.narrative:
General Matter is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Scott Nolan and Lee Robinson that has raised $50M+. The valuation analysis triangulates across a comp universe of 11 peers (3 public, 8 private) in the nuclear energy sector, including same-stage and adjacent-stage companies such as Fuse Energy, Valar Atomics, Nano Nuclear Energy, Helion, and X-Energy.

Two methods were applied to establish a valuation range. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $50M total raised as a proxy for Series A entry value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of A-to-next-stage progression, implies a valuation of $100M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $808M. The peer sample spans $200M (Fuse Energy, Series A) to $6.0B (Valar Atomics, Series B), establishing meaningful context for General Matter's likely position.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $85M to $929M, with a median of $454M across both methods. The wide range reflects material uncertainty in early-stage nuclear venture positioning: stage-progression conservatively suggests $85M–$100M, while peer-median implies significantly higher value at $808M. Key uncertainties include General Matter's technology differentiation relative to Fuse Energy and other Series A peers, the trajectory and milestones required to justify mid-stage multiples, and sector-level funding momentum in nuclear energy capital markets.
